To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have constructed a map from a group of linear combination of pairs of triangles to a group of linear combina- tions of polytopes.

the group of linear combinations (with coefficients in Q) of pairs of triangles considered up to the PGL(3) action with respect to a cut of any triangle is isomorphic (up to 12-torsion) to B2 ⊗ Q ⊕ S2 B1.

the group of linear combinations (with respect to the cutting of triangles of a pair) of pairs of triangles is isomorphic (up to 12— torsion) to B2 ⊗ S2B1; the isomorphism can be constructed in the form of a composition of a map, induced by the Dehn invariant of a pair, and a map, induced from the volume of a triangle of a pair (see Theore m 3.6).
In summary, our research is concerned with
a study of motivic homology and cohomology of projective spaces, and with a description of their relations to the classical homology and co-homology theories.
the study of motivic (co)homology of a plane with two distinguished projective lines and its application to a description of the motivic cohomologies of pairs of triangles.
the construction of a mixed Hodge structure on the motivic cohomologies of a projective space with two families of projective subspaces.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the motivic cohomolgy of a projective line with a distinguished family of projective lines is the group of linear combinations (with integer coefficients) of the classes of the pairs of triangles on the projective plane, considered up to the PGL (3) action with respect to cutting.

a group of all linear combinations of pairs (A, B) of triangles considered up to PGL(3) and cutting of triangles A and B is isomorphic to the group of all linear combination of pairs (A,B) of triangles on a sphere with the same properties.
the motivic cohomologies of the plane are isomorphic up to torsion to the tensor product of the Bloch group and the symmetric square of a multiplicative group.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the group of linear combinations up to cutting of pairs of triangles is isomorphic to a subgroup in the group of linear combination of polytopes up to cutting.
the Dehn invariants of a pair of triangles on the plane are the analogs of Aomoto dilogarithms.
the group of linear combinations up to the cutting of pairs of triangles is a subgroup in the group of linear combination up to the cutting in the plane.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the motivic cohomolgy of PGL(2, K) with coefficients in K (0, 2) is isomorphic to the group of linear combinations (up to PGL(3, K) of pairs of triangles considered up to cutting of any of the triangles.
this isomorphism is given by the Aomoto dilogarithm and the mixed Hodge structure on the Bloch group (Theorem 2.12).
the motivic cohomological theory of a pair of triangles on a projective plane is a nontrivial extension of the classical Dehn invariant theory of a single triangle on a plane.
